title: Situation backup
headline: The backup shows the SWOT detail, five named rivals plus Mega Bangna, and the team's BCG and nine-box views; malls rank first and offices sit at Low x Low.

items.head: Strengths
items.text: Center of Life brand; 44 centres (FY2025; 45 by Q2 2026), 16 community malls, 23 provinces; about 510 million visits a year; The 1 data; events.

items.head: Weaknesses (team observations, not cited)
items.text: Reliance on physical retail; cost of a premium experience; uneven needs by location; scale versus agility; high expectations.

items.head: Opportunities
items.text: Tourism beyond China; experience economy; The 1 personalisation; Net Zero by 2050 and the sustainability-linked bond; mixed use; Thai SMEs; creators.

items.head: Threats
items.text: E-commerce, social commerce; Siam Piwat, The Mall Group; household debt 85.9% of GDP (Q1 2026); China arrivals -33.55% in 2025, +16.05% Jan–Aug 2026.

columns.title: Five rivals, plus Mega Bangna (CPN-linked)
rows: Ultra-premium and luxury; tourist and Gen Z focus
About 70% of luxury spend, single-source estimate
Family and mass market; upgrading to a more affluent catchment
Small and private; competes on novelty
About 35 branches; often a tenant in CPN malls
Ikano Centres with Siam Future Development
Siam Future Development is a CPN subsidiary

columns.title: Reading the two views
items: Both are portfolio tools (which business line to fund), so they sit in backup, not in the core deck.
Both are team assessments, not CPN statements.
Malls are the only Star and the only High x High cell; hotels and residential sit in the Selectivity band.
Offices sit at Low x Low (bottom-right): a stable earnings line and the lowest capital priority of the four.

columns.title: Prime retail market, Q3 2026
columns.text: Central Retail District, prime: average asking rent ฿3,769 per sq m a month, stable on Q2; vacancy 3.63%, down from 3.98% in Q2; rental growth 1.40% y/y. These are market figures, not CPN rents.

columns.title: Footnote: The Central Phaholyothin date
columns.text: CPN's October 2025 release targeted Q4 2026 and the One Report (p. 30) lists December 2026. The 2Q26 MD&A (p. 7) lists "The Central" at 1Q27 with about 100,000 sq m, which the team reads as The Central Phaholyothin. Cushman & Wakefield's Q3 2026 report (p. 2) still lists "The Central" (152,000 sq m) for Q4 2026. The team uses 1Q27, its reading of the MD&A line.

notes: Backup slide, not presented. SWOT and rivals are from the Section 2 text as corrected on 29 Oct 2026; the Threats figures match Table 6.6 in Chapter 6: China arrivals fell 33.55% in 2025 and rose 16.05% in January to August 2026 (year-on-year changes, not a fall from the pre-pandemic peak, for which the report has no figure), and household debt was 85.9% of GDP at Q1 2026. BCG and nine-box views are team assessments from the Week 6 appendix; Offices sit at Low x Low (bottom-right). The footnote lists the dates CPN and Cushman & Wakefield give for The Central Phaholyothin.

facts.on_slide: household debt 85.9% of GDP (Q1 2026)
facts.meaning: Thai household debt as a share of GDP at Q1 2026, the latest figure the team confirmed; a six-year low that SCB EIC attributes to restricted credit access, not to stronger household finances. Section 2 of the report gives the same 85.9%, with 86.7% at Q4 2025 in brackets. Economic slowdown threat

facts.on_slide: China arrivals -33.55% in 2025, +16.05% Jan–Aug 2026
facts.meaning: China arrivals to Thailand fell 33.55% in 2025 (a year-on-year fall) and rose 16.05% in January–August 2026. Neither is a fall from the pre-pandemic peak, and the report gives no peak figure. Section 2 of the report now gives the same two figures (its earlier 'about 30% below peak' wording was replaced on 29 Oct 2026)
